help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:106  Naming more than one destination serves **one** dashboard with the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:107  reports merged row by row: a session held by several destinations is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:108  listed once, with a badge saying how many copies there are, and the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:109  counts are printed both ways (distinct sessions and raw copies). The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:110  destinations are read in the order named, and where two copies of a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:111  session disagree the first one named supplies the row — so the order is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:112  a choice, not an accident, and the narration prints it back.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:360  Is the scheduled archive actually working? Plus what the local harness
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:361  scanner finds (read-only). Add `--destination` to list archived writer
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:362  versions and identify machines behind the newest writer.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:363
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:364  The first line answers the question the timer cannot: it reads the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:365  `run-state.json` written by the last `run-once` pass. Three distinct
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:366  answers, and only the first is a healthy one:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:367
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:368  * last run recent and successful -> exit 0
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:369  * last run FAILED -> exit 1, saying which step failed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:370  * no run recorded at all, or nothing has run for longer than
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:371    4x `backup_interval_secs` (minimum 1 hour) -> exit 1. A dead timer
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:372    usually leaves a *successful* last run behind, so this overdue check
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:373    is the only thing that catches it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:374
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:375  Never prints session content: counts, timestamps and digests only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:376
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:377  Default output is a handful of lines and nothing more: the verdict
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:378  above, then aggregate scan counts (per-harness session totals, skipped
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:379  roots, unarchivable-session warning). It stays that size whether the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:380  machine holds three sessions or three thousand, so the verdict never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:381  scrolls away.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:382
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:383  `--sessions` adds the per-session metadata table on top of that —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:384  one line per session (harness / bytes / mtime / first 8 chars of the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:385  id). That is the troubleshooting view; it can be hundreds of lines.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:387  Also print one metadata line per session found (can be hundreds).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:390  Print exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else (the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:391  human lines still go to stderr). Tri-state fields are tagged
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:392  `{"kind":"known",…}` / `{"kind":"unknown","why":…}` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:393  `{"kind":"not_applicable",…}` — an unknown is never serialised as
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:394  `0`, `null` or a missing field. `run_state.kind` is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:395  `known` / `missing` / `unreadable`; `scanner.kind` is `ok` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:396  `failed`. `exit_semantics` documents what the exit code means.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:418  Dump one session back from the repository (sequence-concatenated) and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:419  print its sha256 for verification — or, with `--all-machines`, walk

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:423  Local stage directory to compare the read against. Optional: the

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:474  Print exactly one JSON object to stdout and nothing else. Tri-state

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:483  Prove the archive is intact. Three independently runnable levels:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:484  l1 = rustic structure check (cheap, no payload reads), l2 = rustic content

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:509  Masterkey file override.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:518  Keep the ssh ControlMaster processes open after this run (do not shut them down).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:522  Initialise a new destination as a *full extra copy* (ADR-013).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:523
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:524  Order is fixed: re-collect from the local sources first (they are the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:525  truth, and rereading them puts no load on an existing destination),
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:526  then copy back only what an existing destination holds and the local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:527  source no longer does, then push the result. The new destination ends
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:528  up with `local ∪ existing destinations`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:529
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:530  A source destination that cannot be consulted makes the difference set
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:531  *incomplete*: that is reported and the command exits non-zero. It is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:532  never treated as "that destination had nothing extra".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:534  Destination to initialise. Must be declared in the config, unless
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:535  an explicit `--repo` is given instead.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:538  Stage directory that holds the sealed `sessions/` tree.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:541  Machine partition for `sessions/<machine>/…`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:544  Maximum sealed shards per bucket (default: 20).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:547  Existing destination to compute the difference set against,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:548  repeatable. Default: every other destination in the config.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:551  Repository path override for the destination being initialised.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:554  Masterkey file override for the destination being initialised.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:557  Concurrency cap override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:560  Backend option `key=value`, repeatable.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:563  Keep the ssh ControlMaster processes open after this run (do not shut them down).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:566  Record this destination's ssh host key in `~/.ssh/known_hosts` after
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:567  printing its fingerprint. Off by default and never implied: without
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:568  this flag nothing is ever written to `known_hosts`, so the first
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:569  connection of an unattended run cannot silently trust a host.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:573  Search one destination's archive by session metadata.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:574
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:575  Metadata tier only: this walks snapshot/index/tree objects plus each
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:576  machine's small activity index, and never fetches or decrypts a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:577  session's conversation shard, which is why it is cheap. On a local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:578  three-session fixture the metadata walk read 11,761 bytes against
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:579  1,206,285 bytes of data packs — two orders of magnitude apart.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:580  In a separate metadata-only run, use `--cost` to estimate the payload
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:581  size before choosing a full-text mode. `--scan` reads those payloads;
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:582  `--text` uses the local index and checks that it covers the selected
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:583  sessions before treating zero hits as a complete answer.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:584
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:585  One destination per run, always named: there is no automatic merge
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:586  across destinations, and no default destination to search "everything".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:587
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:588  The time window filters on the **conversation's own activity interval**,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:589  not on when the backup ran: a session matches when `[first message,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:590  last message]` intersects the window. Those times come from the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:591  `activity-index` sidecar (`meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl`) carried in
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:592  the archive, so `--day 2026-01-15` finds a conversation held that day
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:593  even if the machine was last pushed months later.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:594
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:595  A session whose conversation time is unknown is **never silently
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:596  excluded**. It is listed separately with the reason, and while a time
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:597  window is active it does not count as a match — which also means a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:598  "0 matched" answer cannot be trusted while any remain, so the exit code
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:599  is `3` rather than `1`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:600
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:601  `--text` searches the local FTS5 trigram index (substring matching for
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:602  runs of at least three characters). One- and two-character queries
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:603  return no FTS matches and suggest a longer query. `--scan` instead
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:604  reads selected conversations and performs a case-insensitive substring
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:605  match; it can answer short queries but reads archived content.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:606
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:607  Exit codes distinguish the three answers, because two of them look the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:608  same and mean opposite things: `0` matched something, `1` read the whole
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:609  destination and answered for every session and nothing matched, `3`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:610  could not finish — either reading it, or placing every session in time —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:611  so "nothing matched" is unproven. `2` is a usage error, as elsewhere.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:613  Destination to search. Required unless an explicit `--repo` is given.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:616  The shared filters (session / machine / harness / time window).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:619  Search indexed titles and user/assistant text with SQLite's trigram tokenizer.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:622  Read selected sessions and perform a case-insensitive substring scan.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:625  Emit one JSON object on stdout. Metadata searches include separate
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:626  matched / not matched / could-not-be-placed groups; text searches
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:627  include counts for metadata read failures and unplaceable sessions.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:630  Also report what a full-text pass over the hits would cost.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:633  Repository path override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:636  Masterkey file override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:639  Concurrency cap override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:642  Backend option `key=value`, repeatable.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:645  Keep the ssh ControlMaster processes open after this run (do not shut them down).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:649  Write every session the shared selector selects to files.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:650
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:651  One destination per run, always named, exactly like `search` — and the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:652  selection is literally the same code path: `export` writes the sessions
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:653  `search` returns for the same flags, so `search` is the dry run of this
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:654  command with a different name, and `--dry-run` prints the same price
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:655  `search --cost` reports before anything is fetched.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:656
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:657  Layout: `<out>/<machine>/<harness>/<session-id>.jsonl`, each file holding
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:658  that session's archived lines in their native format, byte-identical to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:659  what `read` returns for it. Plus `<out>/manifest.json`: per session its
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:660  machine, harness, id, first and last message time, shard count, bytes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:661  written, sha256 of the written file and the filters that were applied —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:662  and, at the top level, the sessions no filter could place, the machines
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:663  whose activity index could not be read, the sessions that could not be
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:664  written, and the exit status this run returns.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:665
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:666  `--turns user` keeps only the lines that are the user's own messages.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:667  That is answerable only where the harness's format makes it certain (see
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:668  `export::USER_TURNS_HARNESSES`); elsewhere every line is written and the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:669  session records `turns_filter: "not-supported"`. The flag is never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:670  silently ignored and content is never silently dropped.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:671
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:672  `--trim-to-window` drops lines whose own timestamp is outside
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:673  `--day`/`--since`/`--until`. A line whose timestamp cannot be read is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:674  kept and counted in `untimed_lines`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:675
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:676  `--out` must be empty or absent unless `--force` is given. Nothing is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:677  ever deleted, and nothing is ever written outside `--out`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:678
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:679  Exit codes, the same family `search` uses: `0` wrote at least one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:680  session and answered every session the query touched · `1` read the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:681  whole destination and selected nothing · `3` did not finish — part of
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:682  the archive was unreadable, a session could not be placed, or a selected
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:683  session could not be written — so the output on disk is real but
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:684  incomplete, and the manifest says what is missing · `2` usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:686  Destination to export from. Required unless an explicit `--repo` is given.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:689  Directory to write into. Must be empty or absent unless `--force`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:692  The shared filters (session / machine / harness / time window).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:695  Which lines to write: `all` (default), or `user` for only the user's
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:696  own messages — kept only for harnesses whose format makes that
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:697  certain; for any other harness every line is written and the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:698  manifest records `turns_filter: "not-supported"`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:701  With a time window, also drop lines whose own timestamp lies outside
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:702  it. Lines whose time cannot be read are kept and counted in the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:703  manifest's `untimed_lines`. Requires a window.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:706  Write into a non-empty `--out`. Nothing is ever deleted, so files
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:707  from an earlier export stay where they are.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:710  Print the plan and stop: no directory is created and no file is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:711  written.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:714  Repository path override.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:717  Masterkey file override.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:726  Keep the ssh ControlMaster processes open after this run (do not shut them down).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:730  Open the archive dashboard in a browser: totals, the machine × source
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:731  matrix, a weekly activity heatmap, and drill-down into any cell.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:732
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:733  Binds a short-lived HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` with an OS-assigned port
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:734  (never `0.0.0.0`, never a fixed port), prints the URL, optionally opens
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:735  your browser, and exits when idle or on Ctrl+C. Nothing is installed:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:736  no launchd, no systemd, no background process, no resident daemon.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:737
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:738  THREAT, stated plainly: loopback is NOT a security boundary. Every other
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:739  program running on this machine can connect to `127.0.0.1`, so this is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:740  not "safe because it's local". Access is gated by a random token that is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:741  generated fresh on every launch and appears only in the printed URL —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:742  never in a file, never in a log. Requests without that exact token are
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:743  refused (403), and any method other than GET is refused (405). Treat the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:744  URL as a secret for the lifetime of the process.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:745
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:746  Metadata tier: the dashboard and every list are rendered from one read of
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:747  snapshot + index + tree metadata plus the activity sidecar. The only
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:748  conversation text that read carries is each session's one-line label
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:749  (at most 100 characters, recorded in the activity index); a session's
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:750  full conversation is fetched and decrypted only when you click it and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:751  then click "load", and the byte cost is printed before you do. Exit
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:752  codes: 0 served the dashboard — even an archive that holds nothing,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:753  which is served as an honest empty page rather than not starting; 3
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:754  could not finish reading (or no key), and is also the exit status after
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:755  serving an archive that could not be read in full; 2 is a usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:757  Deprecated alias for `ui`; prints a one-line notice on stderr and behaves
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:758  identically. Kept for one release.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:760  Consume ext inbox bundles into sealed staging shards.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:852  Reclaim the sealed shard body from the staging tree, but only where the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:853  archive provably holds every byte (ADR-020 Phase 4).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:854
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:855  The stage is an unbounded local full copy; nothing ever shrinks it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:856  This command retires the shard body once every declared destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:857  proves it holds each session. Proof means asking the archive itself —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:858  never the local cursor — for every session's digest triple (shard
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:859  count / concatenated bytes / concatenated sha256) and matching it
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:860  against the stage. A destination that cannot be consulted is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:861  "unproven" and blocks the reclaim: it is never treated as "does not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:862  have it". Every declared destination must prove it holds each session,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:863  or
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:864  nothing is deleted.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:865
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:866  Default is a dry run that reports what would be reclaimed and deletes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:867  nothing; pass `--apply` to actually remove the body. `--apply` writes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:868  each machine's retained summaries first, then deletes session by
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:869  session, keeping each session's persistent `shard-seq` counter so the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:870  next sequence never falls back onto archived shard names.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:871
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:872  Exit codes: 0 = reclaimable (dry run) or reclaimed (apply); 1 =

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:874  to hold a session, so nothing was deleted; 2 = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:876  Stage directory that holds the sealed `sessions/` tree.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:898  Report the packs one destination's backend holds that **no index file
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:899  names** — what a push killed between its packs and its index strands —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:900  and say what the next push would do about each. Deletes nothing; there
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:901  is no mode in this build that deletes.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:902
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:903  Dry run is the only mode. `--apply` is refused with exit `3`, naming
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:904  what a safe delete would need and this build does not have: a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:905  repository-wide lock every client honors, a conditional delete carrying
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:906  an object version, and a trustworthy backend modification time to age
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:907  candidates by. "Unindexed" means no index file names the pack, not that
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:908  the pack is unused — a retry can reuse one and write a snapshot that
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:909  depends on it while it stays unindexed on disk — so the gap is real, not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:910  a formality.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:911
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:912  Every pack it reports is verified the way the adopting open verifies one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:913  before reusing it: the header must decrypt, every blob it declares must
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:914  decrypt and hash to the id the header gives, and the pack's bytes must
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:915  hash to the id it is stored under. A pack that fails any of those is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:916  reported **unknown** with the verifier's reason, never as empty and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:917  never as zero, and its presence makes the whole survey incomplete.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:918
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:919  Reads only: nothing is written to the repository, to an index file or to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:920  a pack. The report carries the repository fingerprint, the backend
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:921  family, pack and byte totals, the unindexed packs by id prefix and size,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:922  what the next push would adopt, and any pack an index names that the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:923  backend does not list. It never carries a path, a host, a machine or an
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:924  account name, or any conversation text.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:925
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:926  Exit codes: 0 = the survey finished and read every pack; 1 = the survey
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:927  finished and found a contradiction (an index naming a pack the backend
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:928  does not have); 3 = it did not finish reading — a pack or an index file

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:930  for — so no absence in the output proves anything; 2 = usage error.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:964  Register this executable as the browsers' Native Messaging host
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:965  (ADR-014 step 2) — or, with `--uninstall`, remove that registration.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:966
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:967  ADR-014 exists because `chrome.downloads` with `saveAs: false` is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:968  overridden by the browser-level "ask where to save each file before
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:969  downloading" preference, which no extension flag can suppress. At up to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:970  200 backfilled conversations a day that is 200 modal dialogs.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:971
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:972  This is one command instead of the five physical actions Native
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:973  Messaging otherwise costs: it renders the host manifest (`name` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:974  `description` / the absolute `path` of *this* executable / `type:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:975  stdio` / the pinned extension allowlist) and drops it into each
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:976  installed browser's discovery directory. No elevation: everything is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:977  per-user.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:978
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:979  Every path written, left alone, skipped or removed is printed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:980  absolutely. "No error" is not the same claim as "a file landed".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:981
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:982  Idempotent: run it twice and there is exactly one manifest per browser,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:983  byte-identical, exit 0 both times. Exit codes: 0 = at least one manifest
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:984  is in place (or, for `--uninstall`, removal finished), 3 = nothing was
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:985  written because no known browser was found, 2 = usage error (bad host
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:986  name / extension id / relative binary path), 1 = an action failed.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:988  Browser to register with, repeatable. Default: every browser whose
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:989  data directory exists on this machine. Naming one explicitly writes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:990  it even when that directory is absent.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:993  Discovery root override (macOS default: `~/Library/Application
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:994  Support`). This is what makes the command testable without writing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:995  into a real browser directory.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:998  Which OS path layout to use. Default: this platform.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1001  Host binary recorded in the manifest. Default: this executable
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1002  (`std::env::current_exe()`), which is the only value that stays
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1003  correct after `cargo install --force`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1006  Host name override. Chromium's grammar is `[a-z0-9_.]` only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1009  Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave/Vivaldi extension id.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1012  Firefox add-on id (`browser_specific_settings.gecko.id`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1015  Remove the manifests this command writes — and nothing else.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1018  Windows only: skip the `reg.exe` step and only write the JSON.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1021  Stage the browser-spawned host is allowed to write to. Recorded in
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1022  the config as `[native_host] stage`. The directory must already
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1023  exist and be a directory: the host never creates a stage, and a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1024  stage that appears because a host was pointed at it is a stage
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1025  nothing pushes. The edit preserves the config file's comments and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1026  everything else in it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1030  The Native Messaging host process itself.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1031
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1032  Runs the same one-request-one-response loop the browser launch uses:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1033  reads one length-prefixed request frame from stdin, writes one response
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1034  frame to stdout, exits 0. Useful for driving the host by hand before any
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1035  browser is involved. Each process serves exactly one request — the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1036  browser starts one process per message, and the host is built for that.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1037
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1038  Nothing but that one frame may ever reach stdout: Chromium reads stdout
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1039  as a `u32` frame length, so a stray log line is read as a multi-gigabyte
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1040  frame and kills the pipe. Diagnostics go to stderr. A frame that ends
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1041  early (EOF inside the length prefix or the body) is answered with
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1042  silence and a non-zero exit, never with a response.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1043
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1044  `--self-test` prints one line of JSON on stdout and exits 0, unchanged:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1045  it answers "does the host process start at all?" without needing a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1046  request.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1048  Print one line of JSON describing this host, then exit 0.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1052  Build the activity sidecar index for one machine partition (ADR-017).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1053
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1054  Walks `<stage>/sessions/<machine>/<session>/<bucket>/NNNNNN.jsonl`,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1055  concatenates each session's shards in global sequence order, and feeds
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1056  every line through the conversation-time extractor to produce one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1057  `ActivityRow` per session. The rows are written as JSONL to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1058  `<stage>/meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl` — the file the `overview`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1059  command reads back out of a destination.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1060
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1061  With `--rebuild --destination`, every archived session for that machine
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1062  is restored to a temporary child of `--stage`, the full index is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1063  rebuilt, and a new complete snapshot is appended. Existing snapshots
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1064  remain immutable. No snapshot is written until the scan and every
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1065  session restore finish, and only the named machine partition is pushed.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1066  The rebuild is safe to re-run, but each run starts over and is not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1067  resumable. A same-machine snapshot found before publication restarts the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1068  rebuild so the appended snapshot cannot hide that newer session.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1069
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1070  The harness label is inferred from the session directory name: the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1071  canonical archived ids are `<source>.<machine>.<native-id>`, so the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1072  harness is the leading dot-segment (`claude-code.<m>.<uuid>` ->
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1073  `claude-code`); short forms are handled too (`opencode~abc123` ->
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1074  `opencode`, `cursor.d~xxx` -> `cursor`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1075
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1076  Metadata, with one declared exception: the extraction keeps a timestamp
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1077  per line and throws the line away, and — for claude-code sessions —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1078  additionally keeps the capped one-line label the dashboard lists the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1079  session under (the harness's own title, or the head of the session's
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1080  first user line; see the `ui` labels). That label — at most 100
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1081  characters, with its provenance — is the one piece of
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1082  conversation-derived text the metadata tier ever holds. Nothing else is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1083  ever kept, and the report is counts and the output path only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1084
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1085  Exit codes: `0` = the whole partition was read and the index written;
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1086  `3` = the stage could not be read (or reading was interrupted) — nothing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1087  (complete) was written; `1` = every session was read but the index file
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1088  itself could not be written; `2` = usage error. Same family as
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1089  `collect`/`search`: `3` means "did not finish / never started", `1`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1090  means "finished and then failed".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1092  Local stage directory, or an existing workspace directory for a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1093  destination rebuild. Temporary restored shards are removed after
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1094  the new snapshot is written.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1097  Machine partition for `sessions/<machine>/…`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1098  Default: config `machine`, else this machine's identity (generated
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1099  on first use); use `--machine` explicitly to choose the partition.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1102  Explicitly rebuild the complete partition index. The command has
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1103  always rebuilt rather than incrementally patched; this spelling is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1104  provided for repair workflows and makes that intent visible.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1107  Destination to rebuild from and append the repaired snapshot to.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1108  Requires `--rebuild`; either this or `--repo` must be named.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1111  Repository path override for destination rebuilds.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1114  Masterkey file override for destination rebuilds.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1117  Concurrency cap override for destination rebuilds.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1120  Backend option `key=value`, repeatable.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1123  Keep ssh ControlMaster processes open after this run.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1127  Write this machine's display-name declaration (ADR-018).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1128
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1129  Writes `<stage>/meta/<machine>/machine.json` — a `MachineDeclaration`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1130  that carries the human display name, the OS and a first-seen time. The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1131  machine partition is resolved exactly like every other command: config
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1132  `machine` first, then the identity file (generated when missing). The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1133  next `push` archives the whole stage root, so this file rides along.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1134
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1135  The display name is taken from `--display-name` when given; otherwise
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1136  the system's LocalHostName (`scutil --get LocalHostName` on macOS,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1137  `hostname` elsewhere) is used. If neither is available the field is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1138  written **empty** and the command says so — a name is never invented.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1139
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1140  Exit codes: `0` = the declaration was written; `3` = the machine
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1141  partition could not be resolved or the identity is unusable; `1` = the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1142  file could not be written; `2` = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1144  Stage directory to write the declaration into (`<stage>/meta/…`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1147  Human display name for this machine. Default: system LocalHostName.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1151  Give a dead or sold machine a display name (ADR-018).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1152
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1153  Writes `<stage>/meta/<target>/label-by-<local-identity>.json` — a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1154  `LabelRecord` expressing *this* machine's opinion about what `<target>`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1155  should be called. It exists for machines that can no longer declare for
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1156  themselves (sold, dead, in a different building). Each file has exactly
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1157  one writer, so concurrent machines never fight over it; the overview
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1158  shows the label with the latest `written_at_unix`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1159
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1160  Exit codes: `0` = the label was written; `3` = the local identity could
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1161  not be resolved; `1` = the file could not be written; `2` = usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1163  Stage directory to write the label into (`<stage>/meta/…`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1166  Machine id (partition) being labelled, e.g. a 32-hex identity.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1173  Draw the machine × harness activity overview of one destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1174  (ADR-017).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1175
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1176  Opens the destination repository, takes each host's newest snapshot
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1177  (the same cross-machine merge as `read --all-machines`), and for every
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1178  snapshot recursively finds the activity index files at
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1179  `meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl`. The paths carry each machine's own
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1180  absolute stage prefix, so they are matched by the trailing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1181  `meta` / `<machine>` / `activity-v1.jsonl` marker — never by a local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1182  path. The indexes are parsed into overview rows and rendered as a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1183  machine × harness matrix, a time-unknown tally and a width-adaptive
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1184  heatmap. Prints counts, machine names and time spans only — never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1185  conversation content.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1186
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1187  A machine that has a snapshot but **no** activity index is listed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1188  explicitly as "index missing" — it never vanishes silently, because a missing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1189  index is not the same thing as "that machine had no sessions".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1190
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1191  Exit codes: `0` = at least one index was read and rendered; `1` = the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1192  whole repository was read and there is no activity index at all (a real
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1193  "there is none", not a failure to look); `3` = the repository could not

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1209  (read in full, no index anywhere); a failed read (exit 3) puts the

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1213  With `--json`, emit the aggregate summary variant instead of the

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1216  variant is named `"summary"` in the object.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1235  Manage this machine's body cache (ADR-034).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1236
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1237  The body cache holds the conversation bodies a read would otherwise pull
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1238  from a destination again, as the destination's own ciphertext. It is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1239  disposable by design: nothing here is part of the archive, and deleting
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1240  all of it changes nothing except how long the next read takes. Without a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1241  subcommand it prints the location, the quota and the current occupancy,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1242  so a cache you never meant to have is visible before you clear it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1244  What to do; omit to see the current occupancy.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1248  Build or inspect the per-destination local full-text index.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1255  `cache` subcommands.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1258  Delete every cached body block.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1259
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1260  Only the cache directory is touched — never the archive, never a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1261  destination, never a key. Entries are re-fetched from the destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1262  the next time a session is read.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1268  Destination to index. Required unless an explicit repository is given.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1400  The parameters of the remote step, exactly as the caller supplied them.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1401
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1402  Every field here is either a name or a location. **No field can carry a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1403  secret**, and that is the point of the shape rather than an accident of it:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1404  the two credential fields are the *names of environment variables*, which the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1405  wizard writes into the config as `env:NAME` and never resolves itself. So a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1406  secret cannot reach the config file as plaintext, and it cannot reach
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1407  `argv` — where it would be captured by the process list and by any log that
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1408  echoes the command — because there is no flag that would accept one.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1411  Which recipe to write.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1414  SFTP: `ssh://<host>:<port>`. S3: the service endpoint, e.g.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1415  `https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1418  SFTP only: the ssh user.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1421  SFTP only: the private key to authenticate with. Optional — leaving it
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1422  out lets the backend use the ssh agent and its own default keys, which is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1423  a real configuration rather than a gap.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1426  S3 only: the bucket (or container) the repository lives in.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1429  S3 only: the region. R2 is single-region and names it `auto`; another
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1430  S3-compatible service names its own.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1433  Both kinds: the prefix inside the account/bucket that the repository
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1434  lives under. Optional, and omitted rather than defaulted: a prefix the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1435  user did not choose would put their archive somewhere they did not name.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1438  S3 only: **the name of** the environment variable holding the access key
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1439  id. Not the key id itself.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1442  S3 only: **the name of** the environment variable holding the secret
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1443  access key. Not the secret.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1446  Declare that this host's key was checked out of band, which authorizes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1447  recording it in `~/.ssh/known_hosts`. A declaration, not a verification:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1448  nothing here, and nothing anywhere else, can check that the comparison
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1449  happened. Without it the wizard stops at an unknown host and writes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:1450  nothing (ADR-039, rejected option E).
